newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam coffee steady but firm, 120,000T exported.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee steady but firm, 120,000T exported.

text.p: Vietnam robusta coffee prices were a shade softer on Wednesday as the market winds down ahead of the Tet holiday period, but current strong arabica levels are lending support, Southeast Asian traders said.
Vietnamese robusta prices were quoted at $1,150-$1,230 a tonne FOB Saigon port, slightly off from last Friday's levels of $1,240-$1,250.

But a trader in Thailand said fundamentals were still firm with the strong Arabica market providing some support. "The arabica market is very tight and that may have helped pull robusta levels up," said the trader.
"The price differential between the two grades is currently around 73-74 (U.S.) cents a pound and that may widen to around a dollar," he said.

He estimated that Vietnam has committed total sales close to 170,000 tonnes this season with about 120,000 tonnes already exported. He said Vietnam has between 100,000 to 130,000 tonnes of coffee still to be exported.
Traders said ports in Vietnam remain congested.
One trader reported that heavy rains earlier this week have delayed the shipment of a 4,600-tonne cargo bound for Algeria.
"The shipment of coffee is wet," said the trader. "Demurrage costs would be expensive."
In a government to government deal concluded in December, Vietnam agreed to sell $9.0 million worth of coffee to Algeria in return for debt cancellation.

Thai coffee prices were quoted at $1,350-$1,380 a tonne. Most regional traders pegged Brazilian output at 20 million tonnes this year. One trader said the latest estimate would add support to the market as Brazil is expected to consume between 11-12 million tonnes domestically, leaving just eight million tonnes for export.
"As we do not see any immediate exports from Indonesia, Brazil, Central America or Colombia, prices should be supported in the short term," one trader said.
He said he expected Indonesian coffee exports would total between 400,000-420,000 tonnes this year after the season gets underway in about two months time.
A total of 592 tonnes were traded on the Singapore Commodity Exchange's (SICOM) May, July, September coffee contracts on Tuesday, which settled at $1,428, $1,423 and $1,418 a tonne respectively.
